name: Activate Autonomy
desc: Identify where you want more ownership and learn how to ask for it in a way that builds trust. Leaders reflect on moments of empowerment, pinpoint areas where they want more autonomy, and practice communicating their ask clearly and confidently. This session explores whether autonomy is earned or given—and how to navigate that tension to create a better workplace experience for everyone.

name: Adapting to Change
desc: Develop your ability to adapt and thrive through change. Leaders reflect on past, present, or future transitions—identifying their own motivation to engage rather than resist. Together, they build a personal plan to move forward and own their growth through the change, turning uncertainty into intentional action.

name: Adapt Your Strengths
desc: Recognize your strengths and adapt them to meet the demands of the moment. Leaders explore what strengths look like in practice, reflect on current challenges, and identify which default strengths are helping—and which might need to shift. The key insight: overcoming challenges starts with leveraging what you already do well, not fixating on gaps.

name: Beat Imposter Syndrome
desc: Rewrite the internal monologue that feeds self-doubt. Leaders learn to separate their achievements from their sense of value, face new challenges with courage and self-compassion, and practice becoming their own biggest advocate. This session helps people recognize that feeling like a fraud is more common than they think—and that growth and competence can coexist.

name: Build Trust on Your Team
desc: Create an environment where trust flourishes and team members collaborate effectively. Leaders complete a Trust Audit to surface where trust might be lacking, explore the three building blocks of trusting relationships (ICE), and develop a plan to strengthen connection with specific individuals on their team.

name: Candid Communication
desc: Communicate with others in a straightforward, clear way while inviting their perspective. Leaders learn how to address needs instead of problems, understand how directness actually strengthens relationships, and work through the obstacles that keep them from saying what needs to be said.

name: Career Mapping
desc: Identify one meaningful step that brings you closer to your overall vision of success. Leaders clarify what they’re working toward, map the gap between where they are and where they want to be, and commit to a specific next move that creates real momentum in their career.

name: Coaching Essentials
desc: Develop the skills to guide meaningful, supportive conversations. Leaders reflect on how coaching from others has shaped their growth, explore the difference between coaching and directing, identify everyday coaching moments, and practice the double diamond coaching questions framework to unlock potential in their people.

name: Constructive Conflict
desc: Understand your natural response to conflict and learn how to help others manage theirs. Leaders explore what productive conflict looks like using the FIRE framework, reflect on situations where conflict was resolved well, and develop strategies to shift the culture of conflict on their team from destructive to constructive.

name: Cross-Cultural Collaboration
desc: Recognize and adapt to cultural differences that shape how teams collaborate and communicate. Leaders explore real-world cross-cultural interactions, reflect on personal assumptions and communication styles, learn key cultural dimensions, and develop actionable strategies for navigating differences with empathy and curiosity.

name: Cultivating Gratitude
desc: Integrate small, meaningful practices of gratitude into your everyday life. Leaders reflect on what they’re grateful for right now, share appreciation with colleagues, explore the three aspects of gratitude, and choose a personal gratitude practice to carry forward—building a more joyful and connected mindset over time.

name: Curiosity in Conversations
desc: See the whole person behind every team member by applying curiosity to your conversations. Leaders practice identifying differences and commonalities, reflect on what truly motivates others at work, and explore what unlocks when you understand people holistically—not just as the role they fill.

name: Decision Making
desc: Strengthen your ability to make decisions aligned with your people, purpose, and principles. Leaders acknowledge the emotions that influence their choices, map the types of decisions they face, and learn to apply personal 3P filters to upcoming decisions—building consistency and confidence in how they lead.

name: Deliberate Listening
desc: Unlock the power of intentional listening by focusing your mind, space, and body on helping others feel seen. Leaders audit their physical environment for distractions, practice asking for what others need to hear, and build awareness of how body language shapes the messages they send—and the trust they build.

name: Deliver Feedback
desc: Deliver feedback in a way that strengthens relationships, builds trust, and drives growth. Leaders learn the two key components of effective feedback—continuous and conversational—explore the SBIR model (Situation–Behavior–Impact–Response), and practice making feedback feel safe and trust-building through real workplace scenarios.

name: Develop Your Leadership Brand
desc: Identify the values and strengths that define you and use them to shape an authentic leadership style. Leaders reflect on leaders who’ve impacted them, discuss what great leadership looks like in practice, and learn how aligning values with action creates a personal brand that earns trust and inspires others.

name: Develop Your Team
desc: Make your team indispensable by identifying strengths, addressing gaps, and crafting a development plan. Leaders reflect on who’s ready for a new challenge, learn the 3 P’s of development, and explore how to align personal growth with organizational needs—unlocking untapped potential across their team.

name: Emotional Intelligence: Self-Regulation
desc: Identify strategies to strengthen your self-regulation in emotionally charged situations. Leaders reflect on moments they wish they’d handled differently, explore how Emotional Intelligence creates space between feeling and responding, and learn three practical steps to respond more calmly and intentionally under pressure.

name: Executive Communication
desc: Refine your communication to better resonate with senior stakeholders. Leaders reflect on recurring messages they want to improve, learn and apply the AFCI framework to sharpen their delivery, and work in pairs to test changes and gather real-time insights that fuel stronger communication habits.

name: Finance for Better Decisions
desc: Recognize the financial impact your decisions have on broader business objectives. Leaders build financial literacy by learning to read Profit and Loss statements and balance sheets, and practice identifying how everyday decisions connect to the overall health and performance of the business.

name: Foster Belonging
desc: Create safety on your team by modelling the building blocks of belonging: value, connection, and support. Leaders reflect on their own experiences of belonging, discuss its impact at work, learn the three building blocks—and practice creating space for vulnerability that makes people feel seen, heard, and included.

name: Habits for Resilience
desc: Create habits that help you withstand challenges and combat stress, anxiety, and overwhelm. Leaders reflect on what brings versus drains energy, discuss the need for regular and intentional rest, and design a personal resilience ritual—moving from reactive survival mode to sustainable, grounded leadership.

name: Hopes, Fears, and Expectations
desc: Clarify hopes, fears, and expectations to build a strong foundation for working relationships. Leaders discuss how sharing openly creates alignment, then practice the exercise themselves—surfacing what matters most to each person and creating the psychological safety that makes great collaboration possible.

name: Inclusive Leadership
desc: Lead with inclusivity by engaging in deeper conversations and uncovering hidden assumptions. Leaders share incorrect assumptions others make about them, develop empathy for those who feel excluded, and explore the three pillars of inclusion—building practical skills for making everyone feel they belong.

name: Inspire with Vision
desc: Establish a vision and align your team to move toward it together. Leaders reflect on how they came to believe in their organization’s vision, learn the 3C’s of communicating vision, and create a plan for regularly sharing progress, celebrating wins, and collecting feedback as the team works toward a shared future.

name: Lead Effective Meetings
desc: Plan and lead meetings that stay focused on the most important outcomes. Leaders explore the three key elements of effective meetings, practice planning a new meeting using those elements, and brainstorm how to improve an existing meeting they lead—so every conversation drives clarity, not confusion.

name: Leading Others Through Change
desc: Support your team through change by creating space for concerns and guiding them toward the future. Leaders learn to act as a filter during transitions, provide psychological safety for the emotions that come with change, and complete a change audit to help specific team members adapt and move forward.

name: Magnify Strengths in Others
desc: Recognize strengths on your team and help people use them to create greater impact. Leaders explore how developing strengths affects individuals, teams, and organizations, learn to define strengths using the 3C’s framework, and create a plan to support and utilize a specific team member’s unique abilities.

name: Make the Most of 1-on-1s
desc: Guide and empower your team with 1-on-1s that build trust, clarity, and momentum. Leaders reflect on what’s helped them feel connected to past managers, identify who on their team needs more connection, and learn the essential elements that turn routine check-ins into high-impact conversations.

name: Manage Your Time
desc: Protect your time for what matters most by grounding priorities in people and purpose. Leaders identify who’s most impacted by their work, define their role’s true purpose, explore the Eisenhower Matrix, and develop strategies for protecting priorities—so the important work doesn’t get buried by the urgent.

name: Peer Coaching
desc: Strengthen your coaching skills by practicing with peers while receiving insights on your own challenges. Leaders reflect on a current challenge, coach and receive coaching through structured practice, share observations and discoveries, and leave with concrete next steps—all in a connected, supportive environment.

name: Performance Discussions
desc: Lead successful and constructive performance discussions that reduce anxiety and build trust. Leaders explore how their team currently feels about reviews, share what makes these conversations hard, learn the pillars of effective performance discussions, and create a plan to implement them—turning evaluations into growth opportunities.

name: Practicing Self-Awareness
desc: Cultivate self-awareness to improve decision-making, strengthen relationships, and lead with empathy. Leaders reflect on when they feel most authentically themselves, learn how self-aware leaders benefit their teams, and explore the two dimensions of self-awareness: knowing who you are and understanding how you show up.

name: Preventing Burnout
desc: Identify the risk factors that contribute to burnout and develop strategies to prevent them. Leaders define what burnout looks like, complete a Personal Burnout Audit, discuss common burnout factors, and uncover strategies to address the root causes—before stress shifts from motivating to harmful.

name: Setting and Achieving Goals
desc: Take an existing goal and make it more achievable. Leaders revisit a goal they need help with, understand the “why” behind it, evaluate it through the SMART framework with fresh eyes, and ask the group for help overcoming limitations—turning vague intentions into actionable plans.

name: Setting Clear Expectations
desc: Create a strong team culture by identifying key values and needs that everyone requires to succeed. Leaders explore attributes that shape team dynamics, articulate the tone they want to cultivate, discuss how norms reinforce that tone, and learn to model the behaviors and attitudes that define how their team operates.

name: Strategic Thinking
desc: Elevate your thinking to tackle complex problems and develop strategies that drive team success. Leaders reflect on what makes a great strategic thinking partner, discuss the importance of zooming out, share a specific problem they want to approach more strategically, and begin crafting a plan—together.

name: Successful Delegation
desc: Sharpen your delegation skills and create space for your most essential work. Leaders complete a delegation audit, discuss common barriers and how to overcome them, and learn the CAMP framework for effective delegation—freeing up bandwidth while building capability across the team.

name: The Art of Recognition
desc: Unlock your team’s best work through tactful, meaningful recognition. Leaders reflect on their team’s current culture of appreciation, learn the difference between reward-based and behavior-based recognition, and create a plan to recognize someone on their team—in a way that’s regular, specific, and genuinely motivating.
